profile.headline: Data Analyst & ML Engineer — MSc Big Data Management and Analytics, Griffith College Dublin. I build end-to-end pipelines: messy raw data in, calibrated and explainable predictions out.
profile.summary:
I'm a data and machine learning engineer based in Dublin, finishing an MSc in Big Data Management and Analytics at Griffith College Dublin after a Higher Diploma in Computing and a BEng in Electronics and Computer Engineering.

My dissertation, StationSafe, predicts Dublin Bikes station stock-outs an hour ahead from 51M+ rows of historical data, live APIs and weather — XGBoost at 0.975 AUC, explained with SHAP and served through a live Streamlit dashboard. I care about the unglamorous parts that make models trustworthy: clean data, leak-free time splits, calibrated probabilities and honest evaluation.

I've also built streaming pipelines with Kafka, Spark and Cassandra, cloud apps with FastAPI, MongoDB and Azure, and BI dashboards in Tableau and Power BI.

projects.title: StationSafe — Dublin Bikes Stock-Out Prediction
highlights: XGBoost classifier that predicts whether a Dublin Bikes station will run out of bikes or docks within the next hour, evaluated on a held-out 2026 test set.
Built the data pipeline from 66 raw CSVs across two schema eras: a station ID crosswalk (116 of ~120 stations matched), Parquet conversion cutting ~4–5 GB to ~300–500 MB, and 37 time-aware features.

Used a chronological split (train 2019–24, validate 2025, test 2026) to avoid temporal leakage; XGBoost (0.975) beat Random Forest (0.970) and Logistic Regression (0.947). Chose class weights over SMOTE given 5.6M training rows.
Live Streamlit dashboard with SHAP per-prediction explanations, JCDecaux and Open-Meteo feeds, and a GitHub Actions job collecting live station data every 15 minutes.
